scope: Startup/shutdown raw+optimized: fill all four window slots, root registration followed by rejected Open unwinds, release capacity and reattach; queue Open before StopAdmission and prove CANCELLED, reject new Init, then drain and restore OS/guards/ownership.

Blitter raw+optimized: real desktop scroll with one hardware list and pending read/write. Quiesced fault releases scene/client ownership and returns; unquiesced fault parks reset-required with live scene token, registration and borrowed read retained.

Two-client timing: 100 paced motion observations and 30 clicks per idle/scroll/physical-disk load, independent application computes/repaints 31 times. Same image unobserved replay has identical event destinations/positions, scanout hashes and update count.

Main measured/unobserved images include final IRQ routing and admission unwind, but precede the StopAdmission gate. That gate only runs during shutdown; raw/optimized shutdown/fault and FASTEST125 runs exercise it separately.
FASTEST125 uses a focused disk-load run with final shutdown gate; reported separately from 100-motion/30-click timing samples.

Measured native IRQ elapsed share covers entry through source routing, excluding final scheduler/RTI; it is not full CPU utilization. Cursor-call elapsed includes preemption/waits. PAL scanout observations are upper bounds.

DT3 matched full-screen echo regression passes and its minimum electrical phase/negative controls remain separate records; DT4 outline/repair targets remain open. Final two-client pointer p95/max and disk button max also fail their proposed UI targets.
No sampling frequency/phase decoding change. This is development evidence, not physical-device or whole-system qualification.
